Yes. A wrong notice can be used against you. Martin’s “everyone does it” line does not rewrite 11.2.

If 11.2 really is: written notice specifying the failure, then 30 days to cure, *then* default or delay damages — that sequence is the leverage. Skip it and Nexagrid can argue:

1. **The clock never started.** A letter that declares default and invoices LDs now may not count as an 11.2 notice. You think you are in enforcement. They say you never gave a proper cure notice.
2. **You jumped a condition precedent.** If you withhold, terminate, or sue on “default” that is not ripe, they claim *you* breached — wrongful default, repudiation, bad faith.
3. **You handed them the exhibit.** Their counsel will wave the letter: you demanded remedies the contract says you cannot have yet.

Firm is fine. False is not. You can be hard today without giving them that gift.

I am not your lawyer, and I am not Gibson & Sterling. If Martin has another clause that actually allows immediate default, he should cite it. If he cannot, do not let “standard leverage” talk you into a defective notice.

Below is a notice you can send *today*: it specifies the failure, starts the 30 days, and tells them exactly what happens if they do not cure. It does **not** declare present default or demand LDs as due now.

**[Date: 22 August 2026]**

**VIA [method required by the Agreement — email / courier / both]**

**[Notice address in the contract]**  
Nexagrid [Legal Name]  
Attn: [notice contact]

**Re: Notice of Failure to Perform — Phase 2**  
**[Agreement title, dated [date]] (the “Agreement”)**  
**Section 11.2**

Dear [Name]:

This is written notice under Section 11.2 of the Agreement.

Under the Agreement, Phase 2 was due on **[8 August 2026]**. As of the date of this notice — fourteen days after that date — Phase 2 has not been completed or delivered. No adequate substitute performance has been provided.

That failure is specified for purposes of Section 11.2.

**Demand to cure.** Nexagrid is required to cure the failure specified above within **thirty (30) days** of this notice, by completing and delivering Phase 2 in full accordance with the Agreement.

**If Nexagrid does not cure within that period,** we will be entitled, without further notice except as the Agreement requires, to:

- declare Nexagrid in default;
- recover delay damages / liquidated damages as provided in the Agreement; and
- exercise any other rights and remedies available under the Agreement or at law.

All rights are reserved. Nothing in this notice is a waiver, election of remedies, or limitation of damages. This notice is given without prejudice to any other failure, past or continuing.

Please confirm receipt in writing and, by **[date 5–7 days out]**, provide a written cure plan with a completion date inside the Section 11.2 period.

Very truly yours,  

**[Your company]**  
**[Name, title]**  
cc: [internal]; Gibson & Sterling (if that is your practice)

---
